issues.legal_issue: When a statutory appeal is entertained and decided on its merits, the limitation period for executing the decree runs from the appellate decree that supersedes the lower-court decree.
material_facts: A final decree was made in a partition suit, and an appeal against it was entertained and ultimately dismissed on its merits.
A formal decree following the appellate decision was drawn, and an execution application was filed within twelve years of that decree.
The judgment debtors challenged execution as time-barred, and the lower courts rejected that challenge.
issues.conclusion: The appellate decree superseded the lower-court decree, and the execution application was not barred by limitation; the appeal challenging that result was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 136 of the Limitation Act, 1963, the limitation period for execution begins when the decree becomes enforceable. A decree under Section 2(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure may be passed by a trial or appellate court. When a statutory appeal is entertained and decided on its merits, the appellate decree merges with and supersedes the lower-court decree whether it affirms, modifies or reverses it; this applies even where the appeal is a second appeal. The court relied on U.J.S. Chopra v. State of Bombay, V.M. Salgaocar and Bros. Pvt. Ltd. v. Commissioner of Income-tax, and Kunhayammed v. State of Kerala. It distinguished Ratansingh v. Vijay Singh, where an appeal dismissed as time-barred produced no decree and the doctrine of merger did not apply. Article 182 of the former Limitation Act and Section 48 of the Code of Civil Procedure were discussed in explaining the change to the present limitation scheme.

predicates.execution_limitation_dispute: A party disputes whether an application to enforce a decree was filed within the applicable limitation period.
predicates.statutory_appeal_decided_on_merits: A statutory appeal concerning the decree was entertained and decided on its merits, rather than rejected solely as late.
predicates.formal_appellate_decree_drawn: A formal decree was drawn following the appellate court's decision.

issues.definition: When an enforcement-limitation dispute involves a statutory appeal decided on its merits and a formal appellate decree, the limitation period runs from that appellate decree.
